purple.note: Pinned by the client brief. Borders, link underlines, drift symbols, default key cap. Not for solid fills under white text.

purple-fill.note: Solid purple under white text. Exists because #7c5cff only reaches 4.35:1 with white.

link.note: Inline links in prose; lighter than the accent so it reads as text on #0f1226. Falls back to purple-fill in light theme.

mint.note: Pinned. Fills, large numerals, icons, borders, glows, focus ring. 3:1 tier.

mint-ink.note: Small text and solid buttons carrying white. Same as mint in dark theme; darkens to #08704f in light theme.

yellow.note: Pinned. Current position, progress, lit indicator, challenge outline, badge dots. 3:1 tier.

yellow-ink.note: Small text (schedule times, labels) and solid buttons. Darkens to #845d00 in light theme.

wine.note: Ground and border of the live/urgent state (.livebar sits on --wine-wash inside a --wine border). Identical in both themes. Never ordinary emphasis; the lit red is --live.

card.note: Pinned flat content surface. Light counterpart #ffffff.

panel.note: Always used as a gradient with panel-hi (#232849, top bevel) and panel-lo (#090b1a, bottom bevel in shadow).

border.note: 1px seam between two parts. border-soft (#22274a) divides rows inside one list.

text.note: Headings and strong text. Ramp down through text-dim (#a8afd6, prose) to text-faint (#8a92bd, mono labels).

screen.note: NEVER flips with the theme. The monitor surface for editor, sample, output, attract screen. Companions: screen-panel #121735, screen-border #2b3160, screen-text #f2f4ff, screen-dim #8d96c4, screen-gutter #6e76ad, screen-mint #2ef2b0, screen-yellow #ffd84d.

screen-well.note: The recess behind a readout or a line-number gutter: one step darker than --screen. Part of the --screen-* set, so it never flips with the theme. Used by .led, .ed__gutter and .attract__out.

live.note: The lamp-family red for anything actually on air: .led--wine and .livebar__dot with its glow. Deliberately not --wine (#b3202a), which is too dark to read as lit on a dark panel. Wine is the housing; --live is the bulb.

hero.purpose: The home headline only. 32px phone to 56px desktop.

body.purpose: All prose at 17px/1.5. Wrapped 68ch in .prose, 62ch in .lede.

body-lg.purpose: Hero sub and page intro paragraphs.

small.purpose: Card blurbs, nav links, list rows, FAQ text.

label.purpose: Every machine label: .silk, .plate, .spec, .badge, footer column heads. Mono 700, tracked.

code.purpose: Editor, samples, output, LED readouts. 15px/1.65, ligatures off, tab-size 4.

display-georgian.purpose: Baloo 2 has no Georgian coverage; :lang(ka) h1-h3 swap to Noto Serif Georgian 700 at line-height 1.22 and letter-spacing 0.

label-14.purpose: Hardware ramp, 14px. Code shown rather than typed: .attract__code, .attract__out, .out__err. One step under the live editor.

label-12.purpose: Hardware ramp, 12px. Numerals struck beside a row: .rules li::before, .schedule time.

label-11.purpose: Hardware ramp, 11px, tracked 0.06-0.13em. The busiest label size: .lamp, .screen__bar, .spec, .lhead__badge, .timeline time, .score__name, the track-card progress label and the impact stat labels.

label-10.purpose: Hardware ramp, 10px, tracked 0.04-0.1em. Captions under a part: .key__sub, .step__n, .levelrow__label, .countdown__label, and the /about swatch and pose captions.

label-9.purpose: Hardware ramp, 9px, tracked 0.09em. The smallest part in the world: .chat__role. Nothing smaller ships and nothing essential is said at this size alone.

led.purpose: Fluid large readout on .led--lg, clamp(1.4rem, 1rem + 1.8vw, 2.1rem), tabular mono with a 9px glow.

step-key.purpose: clamp(0.7rem, 0.5rem + 0.9vw, 1rem) on .step__key so eight caps shrink instead of wrapping.

key-glyph.purpose: The track's stamped mono mark on .key__glyph, 1.45rem, echoed at 1.05rem on .trackcard__cap.

brand.purpose: .marquee__brand at 1.3rem, dropping to 1.1rem at <=680px; its text hides at <=430px.

shadows.name: sh-3
shadows.purpose: The bezel and the open mobile menu.

shadows.name: sh-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover on any clickable card; adds the purple edge ring.

shadows.name: key-bevel
shadows.purpose: The side wall of a moulded key cap. Hover grows to 7px; :active collapses to 1px with translateY(4px).

shadows.name: recess-screen
shadows.purpose: Screens, editor and attract surfaces read as sunk behind glass.

shadows.name: recess-plate
shadows.purpose: The silkscreen plate struck into the cabinet body, with a lip of light beneath it.

shadows.name: recess-led
shadows.purpose: The --screen-well LED recess behind every number.

shadows.name: lit-glow
shadows.purpose: Only on parts that are actually powered: lamp bulb, done/current level cap, XP fill, live dot. LED digits use text-shadow: 0 0 9px currentColor.

shadows.name: shadow-alphas
shadows.value: rgba(0,0,0,.3) cap seat | .45-.5 struck plate and XP track | .75 editor recess | .85 screen recess | .9 LED well | rgba(255,255,255,.05-.5) bevel highlight
shadows.purpose: The bare black and white alphas inside box-shadow and inset declarations in cabinet.css, editor.css and pages.css are depth and sheen, not palette entries, and are intentionally theme-independent: a hole is dark and a moulding edge catches white light in either theme. Reuse one of these depths; never add a new accent rgba() here.

motion.name: e-out
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for reveals, card lifts and cap state changes.

motion.name: d-press
motion.purpose: Button and key press, nav tint, control hover.

motion.name: d-lift
motion.purpose: Card lift 6px, level cap state change, FAQ chevron.

motion.name: d-reveal
motion.purpose: The one authored moment per section: .reveal fades up 24px once on first scroll-in.

motion.name: d-type
motion.purpose: Attract-screen typewriter and the impact counters.

motion.name: xp-reveal
motion.purpose: Progress fills are revealed by clip-path on a full-width gradient, never by animating width.

motion.name: lamp-pulse
motion.purpose: The FREE PLAY bulb and the mascot's antenna. The live dot runs the same keyframes at 1.3s.

motion.name: bit-blink
motion.purpose: Mascot eyes blink every 4s; the right eye lags 0.08s.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion flattens all motion, hides .drift and the attract caret, stops mascot animation, and makes confetti() and the pop return early.

motion.name: confetti
motion.purpose: Fires only on a passed challenge, in the six key-cap colours read from TRACKS[].color in src/lib/fx.js, so recolouring a track recolours the celebration. Returns early under prefers-reduced-motion.

radiusLadder.name: bezel

radiusLadder.name: r-card

radiusLadder.name: step

narrative.overview:
Every part on this site is a piece of arcade hardware. The header is a lit marquee sign, the promise line is a plate struck into the moulded cabinet body, the six track buttons are injection-moulded plastic key caps that genuinely travel down 4px when pressed, numbers are segmented LED readouts behind glass, and the code editor is a monitor sitting inside a dark bezel. Nothing is "a card with an icon on it" — ask what part of a machine it is first, then build that part.

The density is generous, not dense: one idea per block, big friendly shapes, 8px spacing steps, and one authored motion moment per section. The world is loud in colour and quiet in behaviour — things react when touched (press, lift, glow) but nothing moves on its own except the FREE PLAY lamp pulse, the mascot's blink, and the attract screen typing itself.

Two themes ship, dark by default (:root) and light on :root[data-theme='light']. Both themes carry the same parts; only the ground and the ink change. One surface deliberately does not change: the monitor.
keyCharacteristics: Arcade hardware parts, never generic web widgets.
Pinned palette from the client brief; no new hues.
Chunky rounded display type (Baloo 2) against strict tracked mono labels (JetBrains Mono).
Every number is a lit readout, every label is silkscreened mono.
Two type ramps that never mix: prose at 15px and up, hardware mono labels at 14/12/11/10/9px.
A radius ladder from a 26px frame down to a 2px lit bar, picked by what the part physically is.
Phone-first: the 8-step level row scales and never wraps, code scrolls sideways instead of wrapping.
Dark-and-light, but the screen is always dark.

rules.name: The Two-Tier Ink Rule
rules.body: Mint and yellow each ship as a pair. --mint / --yellow are the pinned brief values and are for fills, large LED numerals, icons, borders and glows — anything judged at 3:1. --mint-ink / --yellow-ink are for small text (13px labels, the schedule times, checklist ticks) and for solid buttons carrying white. In dark theme the pair is identical; in light theme the ink versions darken (#08704f, #845d00) because #0f9f72 and #a67600 hold 3:1 on white but not 4.5:1. If you are typing label-sized text or a filled button, reach for the -ink token; if you are filling a shape or drawing a border, reach for the plain one.

rules.name: The Monitor Rule
rules.body: The screen tokens (--screen, --screen-panel, --screen-text, --screen-dim, --screen-border, --screen-mint, --screen-yellow, --screen-gutter, --screen-well) never flip with the theme. A monitor is a monitor; the code box, the sample block, the output pane, the attract screen and the LED readouts stay dark in light theme. --screen-well is the darkest member of the set, the recess behind a readout or gutter. This also means code contrast is identical whichever theme the learner picked. Using --text or --card inside a screen puts dark text on a dark surface — a real bug, not a style preference.

rules.name: The Washes-Not-Tints Rule
rules.body: Translucent accent surfaces come from the existing wash/edge tokens (--purple-wash + --purple-edge, and the mint, yellow and wine equivalents). Never hand-write a new rgba() of a brand colour.

rules.name: The Georgian Display Swap Rule
rules.body: Baloo 2 has no Georgian coverage. :lang(ka) on h1-h3 swaps the display face to Noto Serif Georgian at weight 700, line-height 1.22, letter-spacing 0 — the tighter Latin metrics clip Georgian ascenders. Body text under :lang(ka) uses Noto Sans Georgian, and :lang(ka) .btn drops to 16px in Noto Sans Georgian so labels still fit the pill. Any new display-sized text needs the matching :lang(ka) rule.

rules.name: The Silkscreen Label Rule
rules.body: Machine labels are always JetBrains Mono, weight 700, 13px or smaller, letter-spaced 0.06em-0.17em, in --text-faint on panel. This is the world's silkscreen; it is how a section head, a spec strip, a channel name and a footer column head all announce themselves. Never set a label in the display face, and never letter-space the display face to fake one.

rules.name: The Two-Ramp Rule
rules.body: There are two type ramps and they do not mix. The prose ramp (hero > h1 > h2 > h3 > 18 > 17 > 15px, Baloo 2 and Nunito) carries everything a learner reads as language. The hardware ramp (14 > 12 > 11 > 10 > 9px, JetBrains Mono 700, tracked) carries only machine labels and readouts: silkscreen labels, spec strips, LED digits, step numbers, status bars, role pills. Prose never drops below 15px, and a hardware label is never set in a prose face or size. When adding small text, decide which ramp it belongs to first — that decision also hands you its font, weight and tracking.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change or line up (.led, .spec, .score, the schedule times, the countdown) carries .tnum or font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits do not jitter as they tick.

rules.name: The Clip-Not-Hidden Rule
rules.body: body uses overflow-x: clip, never overflow-x: hidden. hidden makes body a scroll container, which silently stops every position: sticky descendant from sticking — the marquee and the lesson header both die. clip contains overflow without creating a scroll container.

rules.name: The Never-Wraps Rule
rules.body: The 8-step level row is grid-template-columns: repeat(8, 1fr) at every width and scales down instead of wrapping; its caps use aspect-ratio: 3 / 4 and clamped type. Below 620px the step labels hide, but the eight caps stay in one row. Do not add a wrap breakpoint.

rules.name: The Offset-Plus-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every ambient shadow token carries both an offset and a blur. A hard zero-blur shadow is allowed only as the side wall of a part that compresses — key caps, pill buttons, step caps — and it must be paired with a blurred ambient shadow in the same declaration. A flat offset shadow on a card, panel or plate is not in this world.

rules.name: The Lit-Means-On Rule
rules.body: A glow states that something is powered: free play, done, you-are-here, running. Never use a glow decoratively on a resting surface. The lit red is --live (#ff5a63), never --wine, which is the housing around it. Shadow and recess alphas are part of this depth vocabulary rather than the palette: reuse the existing depths (0.3 / 0.45-0.5 / 0.75 / 0.85 / 0.9 black, 0.05-0.5 white) instead of adding a new rgba().

rules.name: The One Moment Per Section Rule
rules.body: A section gets exactly one authored moment: .reveal fades it up 24px once, the first time it scrolls in. Everything else in that section is a response to touch. Confetti fires only on a passed challenge.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Rule
rules.body: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, base.css flattens all animation and transition durations to 0.001ms, .reveal starts visible, .drift is display: none, the attract caret hides, the mascot animations are none, and fx.js returns early from confetti() and the pop. New motion must be reachable by one of those switches, and nothing may be the only way information is delivered.

rules.name: The Smaller-Part-Smaller-Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius follows the size of the part, not taste: 26px a frame, 20px a card, 14px a key or screen, 10px a control, 9px a cap, 8px a well, 6px an inlay, 4px a hairline detail, 2px a lit bar. When adding something, take the rung of the part it physically resembles instead of inventing a value between rungs.

dos: Do build new elements as cabinet parts: ask whether it is a lit sign, a moulded key, a struck plate, a recessed well or a screen, then reuse .panel / .key / .plate / .screen instead of inventing a container.
Do use --mint-ink / --yellow-ink for label-sized text and for solid buttons carrying white, and plain --mint / --yellow for fills, large LED numerals, icons, borders and glows.
Do keep every screen-like surface on the --screen-* tokens so it stays dark in light theme.
Do set every machine label in JetBrains Mono, 700, <=13px, letter-spaced — and add a :lang(ka) rule whenever you add display-sized type.
Do decide which ramp new text belongs to before sizing it: prose (>=15px, Baloo 2 / Nunito) or hardware (14/12/11/10/9px mono), then take the exact step.
Do take a radius off the ladder by what the part physically is — 26 frame, 20 card, 14 key/screen, 10 control, 9 cap, 8 well, 6 inlay, 4 hairline, 2 lit bar.
Do use --screen-well for the recess behind a readout or gutter, and --live (not --wine) for anything that is actually on air.
Do derive decorative colour sets from data that already exists (TRACKS[].color) rather than writing a second palette.
Do space with --s1--s5 and the .stack-* helpers, and keep content inside .wrap (1100px, 16px gutter).
Do reveal progress with clip-path on a full-width fill.
Do keep every number tabular (.tnum) and every count honestly zero.
Do draw new icons into src/components/Icon.jsx on its 24px grid at 1.75 stroke with round caps, filling only genuinely solid objects.
Do test both themes and a keyboard pass: the focus ring is a 3px --mint outline at 3px offset, and it must stay visible on every new control.
donts: Don't introduce a colour that is not in tokens.css, or hand-write an rgba() of a brand colour instead of using a -wash / -edge token.
Don't put --purple (#7c5cff) behind white text — use --purple-fill for solid fills.
Don't use themed tokens (--text, --card, --mint) inside a screen, editor, LED or attract surface; that is how dark text lands on a dark monitor.
Don't change body to overflow-x: hidden; it breaks every sticky element on the site.
Don't make the editor wrap, or add a wrap breakpoint to the 8-step level row.
Don't animate width on a progress fill.
Don't turn Bit's four hardcoded swatches into tokens or theme them; the /about reference sheet names those exact hexes.
Don't invent a radius between rungs of the ladder, put a flat zero-blur shadow on a non-compressing surface, or glow something that is not powered on.
Don't set prose below 15px or a hardware label at a prose size, and don't let 9px or 10px text be the only place a piece of information appears.
Don't add a new rgba() depth to a shadow, and don't read the existing shadow alphas as palette colours — reuse the recess and bevel depths already named.
Don't add a second authored motion to a section, and don't ship motion that reduced-motion cannot switch off.
Don't letter-space Baloo 2 to fake a mono label, and don't set a heading in Nunito.
